questions.code:
ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :jobs do |t|
    t.string :name
    t.integer :priority
  end
end

class Job < ActiveRecord::Base; end

Job.create!(name: "email",   priority: 2)
Job.create!(name: "report",  priority: 5)
Job.create!(name: "cleanup", priority: 3)

puts Job.order(priority: :desc).first.name

query.explanation: Many background-job systems drain a queue by priority rather than insertion order. Here `order(priority: :desc)` sorts the rows from the highest priority value to the lowest, so the row with priority 5 comes first and `first.name` returns "report". Insertion order only matters as a tiebreaker when priorities are equal, which is not the case here.
query.title: Priority ordering in a job queue
